# EnterpriseGlue v0.31.1 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.31.0`.

## Highlights

- **oracle:** Repair historical boolean migration SQL for Oracle releases without SQL BOOLEAN support.
- **backend dependency security:** Remove the vulnerable braces build dependency and upgrade the Spanner SDK to eliminate vulnerable OpenTelemetry dependencies from the backend.

## User and administrator impact

- Existing Oracle application databases can resume pending migrations using numeric boolean storage.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- Install the patch and rerun pending migrations with the schema-owner identity; keep the existing database and migration ledger.
- Build from the frozen workspace lockfile or consume the qualified updated backend image to use Spanner SDK 9.1 and OpenTelemetry 2.x.

## API and integration compatibility

- Public boolean settings and values remain unchanged.
- The shared package optional Spanner peer range accepts SDK 9.1 alongside 8.x; HTTP APIs and configuration schemas are unchanged.

## Configuration

- No new configuration. Native network encryption and SSO retain their existing independent settings.
- Backend build commands and supported runtime configuration retain their existing interfaces.

- Database rollback supported for the combined release: yes.

## Security

- Encryption requirements and authentication/authorization policy are unchanged.
- Remove tsc-alias and its transitive braces 3.0.3 dependency, affected by CVE-2026-93687 (GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm), without suppressing the advisory.
- The braces package was a build dependency and absent from the production dependency graph and both v0.31.0 Oracle image SBOMs.
- Upgrade the Spanner SDK from 8.11.0 to 9.1.0 with its required Google SDK and OpenTelemetry family to remove OpenTelemetry core 1.30.1, affected by CVE-2026-54285 (GHSA-8988-4f7v-96qf), from production dependencies.

## Known limitations

- Physical compatibility was verified on Oracle 21c; acceptance against each deployment's exact Oracle version, identity provider and configuration remains separate.
- Live Google Cloud Spanner acceptance remains separate from the passing emulator qualification.
- Previously published v0.31.0 artifacts remain unchanged; consume the updated release artifacts for the production SDK dependency repair.

## Rollback

- Application rollback retains already applied numeric columns and migration ledger entries; do not delete the ledger or rerun the failing older image.
- Reverting the build-tool change restores the vulnerable development dependency and requires a security assessment.
- Reverting the production SDK upgrade restores the old OpenTelemetry dependency and requires a security assessment; no schema rollback is needed.

## Validation evidence

- 44 focused Oracle SQL-generation, adapter, portability and bridge tests passed. The exact invalid BOOLEAN DEFAULT false DDL is reproduced with TypeORM's actual Oracle compiler; repaired false/true/nullable columns emit numeric SQL.
- 63 database-portability unit tests, migration identifier and raw-SQL guards passed. Shared package build, backend typecheck, database qualification contracts and documentation contracts passed.
- The compiled pending migration passed a populated native Oracle Free fixture: default backfill, preserved settings, numeric true on retry, migration-ledger no-op replay, and rollback. This native fixture is not pre-23 physical acceptance.
- The full five-database CI qualification passed on PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, native AMD64 Oracle 21c and the Spanner emulator, including all seven stages and six supported upgrade baselines. Oracle 21c replay of the actual compiled pending SSO migration verified the numeric default, preserved populated settings, true-value retry and rollback.
- All 3,858 backend unit tests passed. Historical migration test doubles now declare their PostgreSQL connection type while retaining their existing schema assertions.
- All 25 historical migration syntax trees preserve the original non-Oracle semantics after substituting the Oracle boolean helper; the three duplicate legacy bodies previously matched their canonical originals exactly.
- Seven executable resolver fixtures passed, including literal wildcard filename substitution; compiled comparison of 744 emitted files retained the same module targets and application code.
- All 3,850 backend and 1,567 frontend unit tests passed; backend and frontend-host typechecks, lint and packed host-package runtime checks passed.
- PostgreSQL and Spanner emulator 1.5.30 each passed seven stages and six populated upgrade baselines. Live Google Cloud Spanner acceptance remains separate.
- The frozen bootstrap image passed its PostgreSQL 16 bootstrap, idempotence, receipt and drift rejection checks with the refreshed production dependencies.
- Frozen dependency installation, peer validation and npm audit passed with zero advisories.
- Native ARM64 standard backend, Oracle and bootstrap images passed the pinned Trivy 0.72.0 all-severity gate with zero vulnerabilities; actual image dependency checks confirmed Spanner 9.1, absent vulnerable packages and capped incoming baggage.
- Source-level protected PR and merge-queue checks passed, including native AMD64 and ARM64 Oracle encryption/SSO acceptance and all five database adapters. GitHub's default-branch braces advisory is fixed; exact release staging and refreshed publication scans remain separate gates.
- Release-note tooling, package version discipline, documentation boundary, license checks and CI contracts passed. The optional peer boundary requires build and production to use the same explicit supported peer alternative while preserving the public Spanner 8.x/9.1 range; its exact CI-contract path is classified without removing dependency-change acceptance lanes.
